registered_at: see the git commit that adds this file (05/11, +0700)
registered_before: any score of this model or of its rule baselines on the official recordings of LID-DS 2021 is computed
owner_decisions: 01/11: the goal is an ML model that detects blind attacks; rule paths set aside until the ML is decided
01/11: recall >= 95 %, precision >= 95 %, latency <= 3 s; benign-binary flagging and burden as low as possible
05/11: where published work falls short, reason and show the solution; decide on branches failing the novelty test; keep p95 <= 3 s
seen_before_registration: lidds-ml-v1 official result (65.2 %, a different model); all development and CB-DS results of the exploration in validation-evidence/results-20261105/ml-exploration, about 30 decision and branch variants were tried on development with attack labels, so the development numbers are optimistic; every rule-branch official result of v2-v4 on the same recordings, whose design informed the token alphabet. Declared: the official LID-DS 2021 recordings are not unseen for the project; the unseen evidence is the live run and LID-DS 2019

model.token_language_model: per-thread 4-grams over syscall exit tokens: name, plus errno, open mode and first directory, or log2 size / 2 (scripts/analysis/lidds_ml_tokens.py); Witten-Bell backoff to P(name) x P(token | name); window score = mean of the 10 highest per-event negative log-probabilities; every window with events
model.current_ml: reference tree (history 3) and support model of the 249 count features, without fix A, with the live warm-up gate lifted for these 10-60 s recordings (lidds_ml_scores.py --all-windows)

why_the_frequency_branches_stay: they add nothing on LID-DS development (about 1 recall point lost) but they are the only branches that see an attack doing more of what is usual, as in the mprotect and seccomp scenarios of the live campaign; decided before the official split is read
decision: per branch, threshold = moment-Gumbel quantile of the per-recording maximum over the validation recordings at alpha / 3; one window above it fires; no tripwire, novelty gate, vote or two-window rule
selection: the highest development recall among eligible; ties to fewer false alarms. Result, before the official split: alpha 0.0005, development 95.96 % (522/544), 0.56 % (19/3,403), precision 96.5 %, p95 2.37 s; CB-DS 891/891, 2/1,410
verification_levels: to claim recall >= 95 % by the Wilson lower bound the official split needs at least 1,223/1,271; to claim false alarms <= 0.8 % by the upper bound, at most about 50/7,938
reported_only: rule baselines (unseen grams or tokens counts) on development only
novelty_finding: on development the token model fires on 1.1 % of the 53.4 % of normal recordings holding an unseen 4-gram (0.25 % of such windows; 92 % of such attack windows), so it is not an any-mismatch rule; but calibrated counts of unseen grams or tokens reach 97.4 % / 0.41 %, as good as the model, and every first firing window holds an unseen gram: on LID-DS the gain comes from the tokens rather than from probability smoothing. Kept by the owner-delegated decision: a learned, graded model with no hand-written condition, and it stays comparable with the rule baseline in the report
limits: thresholds use 60 validation recordings per scenario: scenario-level false alarms are not verifiable, only pooled
CB-DS has no exploit time: its latency is not meaningful
the tokens need syscall exits, errno, sizes and open paths per thread: not in the live probe; overhead unmeasured; a kernel implementation hashes grams, to be replayed before live
a score is computed in user space from traces
next: official once, then probe and overhead, a blind live run against the stable system with benign-binary flagging and burden measured, then LID-DS 2019 once
